english.title: Carrier - carriage of goods in bulk when prohibited - Dangerous Goods and Pressure Equipment Reg's 07

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) was the carrier of goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), which were in a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) and the carriage of such goods or equipment in bulk was prohibited by the European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Road (ADR) 3.2
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 62(3) of the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes:
Important: these Regulations have been replaced by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009.
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be applied in accordance with HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
